title: Moroccan Braised Lamb Shoulder — Apricot Couscous on Saturday, Crispy Lamb Flatbreads on Sunday
description: One slow oven braise, two dinners: spiced lamb shoulder with apricots, carrots and tomato over couscous with harissa yogurt on Saturday, then crisped in a hot pan and piled onto flatbreads with mint yogurt and a chopped salad on Sunday. Garlic-free.

ingredients.name: Bone-in lamb shoulder (bárány lapocka), or 1.3 kg boneless
Saturday — fresh coriander or parsley, chopped
Sunday — pita or flatbreads (~60 g each)
Sunday — small red onion, thinly sliced

steps.title: Rub the lamb
steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C (fan 145°C). Trim the thickest fat cap off the lamb, then rub all over with the ras el hanout, cumin and salt.

steps.title: Sear the lamb
steps.text: Heat the olive oil in a large lidded casserole over medium-high heat. Brown the lamb on all sides, 8–10 min total. Lift out onto a plate.

steps.title: Soften the vegetables
steps.text: Lower to medium. Cook the onions and carrots in the fat 6 min until soft, then stir in the ginger and tomato paste for 2 min.

steps.title: Build the braise
steps.text: Add the tinned tomatoes, stock, apricots, honey, cinnamon stick and lemon zest. Bring to a simmer, scraping up the browned bits, and nestle the lamb back in — liquid about two-thirds up the meat.

steps.title: Braise in the oven
steps.text: Cover tightly and braise 3 h 30 min, turning the lamb once halfway. Done when a fork twists the meat off the bone with no resistance; give it 30 min more if not.

steps.title: Shred and skim
steps.text: Lift out the lamb, discard bones and fatty bits, and shred into chunks. Spoon the fat off the sauce (this matters for the calories). If thin, boil uncovered 10 min. Remove the cinnamon, add half the lemon juice, taste for salt, and return the meat.

steps.title: Set aside Sunday's portion
steps.text: Weigh out about 420 g shredded lamb with a little sauce for Sunday. Cool and refrigerate within 2 hours; keeps 3 days.

steps.title: Saturday: couscous
steps.text: Pour the boiling water over the couscous with a pinch of salt and the remaining lemon juice, cover 5 min, then fluff with the olive oil and half the herbs.

steps.title: Saturday: harissa yogurt and plate
steps.text: Swirl the harissa through the 100 g yogurt. Couscous 120 g dry weight Matthias / 50 g partner, lamb 260 g / 160 g with sauce, harissa yogurt for Matthias, almonds and remaining herbs on top.

steps.title: Sunday: pickle the onion
steps.text: Toss the red onion with half the Sunday lemon juice and a pinch of salt; leave 10 min while you prep.

steps.title: Sunday: mint yogurt and salad
steps.text: Stir half the mint, a squeeze of lemon and a pinch of salt into the 190 g yogurt. Toss the cucumber, tomatoes, parsley, remaining mint and lemon juice with 10 ml olive oil.

steps.title: Sunday: crisp the lamb
steps.text: Heat the remaining 5 ml olive oil in a large non-stick pan over high heat. Spread the lamb in one layer and leave 3–4 min until crisp underneath, turn and crisp 3 min more. Spoon over a little sauce at the end.

steps.title: Sunday: warm the flatbreads
steps.text: Warm the flatbreads in a dry pan or under the grill, about 1 min per side.

steps.title: Sunday: assemble
steps.text: Mint yogurt ~150 g across Matthias's two flatbreads / ~40 g on partner's one, lamb 260 g / 160 g, then salad and pickled onion. Feta on Matthias's, sumac over everything.

notes: Macros shown are Saturday's. Sunday (flatbreads): Matthias ~1,300 kcal, 105 g protein, 85 g carbs, 55 g fat; partner ~590 kcal, 55 g protein, 42 g carbs, 22 g fat. Greek yogurt is Matthias's protein bridge both nights. Start around 15:00 on Saturday for dinner around 19:30; Sunday takes about 20 min. Kifli swap: lamb shoulder is often out of stock outside Easter — try a market butcher (Lehel, Fény utca) or use 1.3 kg boneless lamb leg (braise 2 h 30 min–3 h). No ras el hanout: 2 tsp cumin + 1 tsp each coriander, paprika, cinnamon.
